findings.title: Unsealed packet modules execute before root validation
findings.stated_guarantee_violated: Unsealed packet-root entries are rejected and a break includes an unsafe filesystem side effect.
findings.why_not_a_documented_boundary: The stable reproducer uses the published verifier unchanged and a non-mutating packet directory; attacker code executes before the promised unsealed-entry rejection. The self-removing PASS variant demonstrates impact but is not required for the unsafe-side-effect finding.

findings.title: Exponent overflow bypasses non-finite JSON rejection
findings.stated_guarantee_violated: The strict JSON parser claims to reject non-finite numbers.
findings.input: Two distinct byte-identical anchor registries with custody_stage: 1e9999
findings.security_scope: The reproduced value is allowed metadata, not a head, key, revocation, or validity decision field; this is a parser-contract and cross-engine differential, not an anchor-selection bypass.

confirmed_defenses: duplicate keys, literal NaN, invalid UTF-8, and deep malformed JSON
derived-file symlink, artifact symlink, hardlink, FIFO, and root extras
anchor disagreement, substitution by same inode, revocation, and validity window

excluded_documented_boundaries: A lying sole OpenSSL executable can validate forged signatures because verifier/host/crypto-engine benevolence is explicitly outside the claim.
Eight MiB of JSON whitespace verifies because JSON whitespace is unsealed and availability has no promised bound.
Concurrent packet mutation, registry freshness and rollback, and hostile-host TOCTOU are explicitly documented external boundaries.

An escaped unpaired surrogate in unused anchor metadata was accepted; retained as a parser-hardening gap, not counted as an exploit because scalar-value rejection is not an explicit guarantee and anchor selection was unchanged.
